intro.en: Floor screeds, tiling, plastering, ceilings, floorings, linings and finishes for specific uses.

text.en: Provide cement-sand levelling screeds to floors where shown on the drawings, laid [[bond]]. Nominal screed thickness shall be [[thk]] mm. Materials, mix and laying shall follow BS 8204-1 unless stated otherwise. Submit the screed mix and a method statement to {{CA}} before work starts.

options.en: bonded to the prepared structural base
floating on an insulation or acoustic layer

hint.en: Project to confirm, varies with bond type

guidance.en: Bonded screeds can be thinner but rely on a clean, keyed base; unbonded and floating screeds need more depth to resist curling and cracking. In HK fit-outs a bonded screed on the structural slab is common, and a thin screed laid over dust or laitance is a frequent cause of hollowness.

text.en: Where floors drain to gullies or channels, form falls in the screed of [[fall]] towards the outlets, with no ponding. Set levels so that outlet gratings sit slightly below the finished floor surface. Where a waterproofing membrane is shown, form the falls in the layer stated on the drawings so the membrane also drains.

guidance.en: Falls are commonly 1:80 to 1:100 in toilets, pantries and plant rooms; flatter falls tend to pond once tile and grout tolerances are added. A frequent HK pitfall is forming falls only in the topping so that water trapped above the membrane cannot escape.

text.en: Protect newly laid screed from rapid drying, direct sun, draughts and early traffic. Cure by [[cure]] for not less than [[days]] days. Do not use curing compounds that would impair the bond of adhesives or floor finishes.

options.en: a curing compound approved by the flooring manufacturer

guidance.en: Summer heat and hot air from temporary ventilation can dry the surface before the screed gains strength, leading to dusting and crazing. Seven days is a common curing period, but the drying time before finishes is a separate and much longer matter.

text.en: The finished screed shall achieve surface regularity class [[sr]] to BS 8204-1, checked with a 2 m straightedge. Grind high spots and fill low spots with a compatible levelling compound approved by {{CA}}. Surface finish shall be [[finish]].

options.en: wood floated, to receive bedded tiling
steel trowelled, to receive adhesive-fixed finishes
lightly textured to receive a levelling compound

guidance.en: Thin finishes such as vinyl, LVT and carpet tiles show every ripple, so they typically need a tighter class than tiles on a thick bed. Agreeing the class early avoids disputes over who pays for smoothing compound.

title.en: Moisture in screeds before floor finishes

text.en: Do not lay moisture-sensitive finishes, including resilient floorings, carpets, timber and adhesive-fixed tiles, until the screed is dry enough. Test moisture by [[method]] and achieve not more than [[limit]], or the lower value set by the finish or adhesive manufacturer. Record the results on a floor plan and submit them to {{CA}}.

options.en: hygrometer test, with electronic meter readings for mapping only

guidance.en: HK's humid climate slows screed drying, so rule-of-thumb drying times are commonly unreliable and testing is the safer basis for release. Where programme does not allow drying, a moisture-tolerant surface membrane approved by the flooring maker is a typical remedy.

text.en: Floor tiles shall be [[type]] tiles to BS EN 14411, absorption group [[group]], nominal size [[size]], colour and finish [[colour]]. Slip resistance shall be not less than [[slip]] as {{ref:FIN-TILE-030}}. Bed tiles by [[bed]] as {{ref:FIN-TILE-060}}. Submit samples of each tile to {{CA}} for approval before ordering.

options.en: as stated in the finishes schedule
as the Material Data Sheet for each tile code

slip.default: the class stated for each area in {{ref:FIN-TILE-030}}

options.v: the class stated for each area in {{ref:FIN-TILE-030}}
options.en: the class stated for each area in {{ref:FIN-TILE-030}}

guidance.en: Porcelain (group BIa) is the usual choice for office and lobby floors because of its low absorption and hard wearing surface. Semi-dry bedding is common in HK for large floor tiles over uneven slabs, while thin-bed adhesive needs a flat screed but gives better contact; state the finish, not just the colour, as polished porcelain is slippery when wet.

text.en: Wall tiles shall be [[type]] tiles to BS EN 14411, absorption group [[group]], nominal size [[size]] mm, colour and finish [[colour]]. Fix with adhesive as {{ref:FIN-TILE-040}} onto a background prepared as {{ref:FIN-PLS-040}}, or onto cement-based board where shown. Submit samples to {{CA}} for approval before ordering.

guidance.en: Glazed ceramic wall tiles are commonly fixed on cement-sand render in HK toilets and pantries; render should be left to cure before tiling. Heavy large porcelain on high walls may need mechanical retention in addition to adhesive, which the designer should consider.

text.en: Floor finishes shall be classified for slip resistance under PNAP APP-175, either by a P class from the wet pendulum test to AS 4586:2013 or by an R class from the oil-wet ramp test to DIN 51130 (the edition cited in APP-175). The two scales are separate and shall not be converted. Minimum classes: indoor regulated routes, toilets, bathrooms and kitchens of residential units [[indoor]]; outdoor regulated routes and entrances exposed to rain [[outdoor]]; commercial kitchens and sculleries [[kitchen]]. Submit independent test reports for each floor finish proposed. Wet pendulum values to BS EN 16165 may be provided as supplementary data for UK-sourced products but do not replace the classification.

guidance.en: APP-175 applies to works consented on or after 1 August 2026 (statutory where in scope, best practice elsewhere). The R12 / P5 kitchen value has no HK source. DIN 51130:2014-02, the edition named in APP-175, has since been replaced by DIN 51130:2023-03.

text.en: Tile adhesive shall be cementitious to BS EN 12004-1, class [[cls]], selected to suit the tile, background and exposure. Use a deformable adhesive (S1 or better) for large-format tiles, external areas and backgrounds subject to movement. Use adhesive and grout from one manufacturer's compatible system, mixed and applied to the manufacturer's recommendations.

guidance.en: Low-absorption porcelain needs an improved (C2) adhesive because ordinary cement-based adhesive bonds poorly to its dense back; T limits slip on walls and E extends open time in hot weather. Mixing products from different makers is a common cause of disputes over failures.

text.en: Grout joints with [[grout]] grout to BS EN 13888-1, colour [[colour]]. Joint width shall be [[joint]] mm, uniform throughout. Clean joints to a consistent depth before grouting and fill fully with no voids.

guidance.en: Cementitious CG2WA grout suits most offices and toilets, while RG epoxy grout is commonly used in commercial kitchens and areas cleaned with chemicals. Butt-jointed tiles leave no room for size variation or movement, so a narrow joint is still typical with rectified tiles.

text.en: Lay tiles only on a base that meets {{ref:FIN-SCR-040}} and, for adhesive bedding, the moisture condition in {{ref:FIN-SCR-050}}. Set out from the centre lines or setting-out points on the drawings so that perimeter cuts are not less than half a tile where practicable, and submit the setting-out to {{CA}}. Bed tiles with full contact and no voids: for thin-bed adhesive use a notched trowel and back-butter large-format tiles; for semi-dry mortar lay on a compacted cement-sand bed with a slurry bonding coat to each tile back. Lippage between adjacent tiles shall not exceed [[lippage]] mm and the finished surface shall be within [[flat]] mm under a 2 m straightedge.

guidance.en: Hollow-sounding tiles are the most common HK tiling defect, usually from semi-dry beds with poor slurry or compaction, or adhesive without back-buttering. Long tiles are rarely perfectly flat, so a half-bond offset tends to show lippage; an offset of one third or less is the usual remedy.

text.en: Provide movement joints at perimeters, at changes of background, over structural and screed joints, and in field areas at not more than [[spacing]] m centres each way, or as shown on the drawings. Joints over structural or screed joints shall pass through the full depth of tile and bedding. Fill with [[filler]] over a compatible backing, colour to suit the grout. Submit a joint layout to {{CA}} for approval.

guidance.en: Omitting perimeter and field joints is a common reason for tiles tenting or popping up, especially where floors are heated by sun through glazing. Prefabricated profiles are typical in heavily trafficked lobbies, sealant elsewhere.

text.en: Where {{CA}} requires, test tiles from delivered batches to the relevant parts of BS EN ISO 10545 at a laboratory [[lab]]. After the bedding has cured, tap-test all tiled areas and replace tiles that sound hollow or are cracked, chipped or loose. Record tap-test results on a floor plan and submit them to {{CA}}.

options.en: with other accreditation, approved in advance

guidance.en: Tap testing with a hard object is the usual HK check for hollowness and is best done before grouting is complete in large areas so defects are cheaper to fix. Batch testing is typically reserved for large orders or where samples and deliveries look different.

text.en: Internal walls and soffits shall be finished with [[system]], to the thickness and tolerance in {{ref:FIN-PLS-040}}. Surfaces to receive tiling shall be left with a scratched or keyed finish and no skim coat.

options.en: cement-sand render with a skim coat
skim coat only on prepared concrete or gypsum board

guidance.en: Cement-sand render with a skim before paint is the common HK system on concrete and blockwork; gypsum plaster is lighter and quicker but unsuited to wet areas. Concrete soffits are often only skimmed, as thick soffit render can delaminate and fall.

text.en: Factory-made render shall comply with BS EN 998-1; site-mixed render shall be cement and sand in the proportion [[mix]] by volume, with admixtures only as approved by {{CA}}. Gypsum plasters shall comply with BS EN 13279-1 and come from one manufacturer's system. Bonding agents on smooth concrete shall be as the render manufacturer recommends.

guidance.en: Pre-bagged render gives more consistent strength than site batching, which commonly varies in sand quality and water content. Bonding agents should be compatible with the render, as a mismatched agent can itself become a plane of weakness.

text.en: Provide [[bead]] angle and stop beads at external corners, edges and junctions with other materials, to BS EN 13658-1 where metal. Fix beads plumb and true with compatible fixings or dabs. Where plaster meets a dissimilar background, form a neat stop or shadow joint, or bridge the junction with mesh as {{CA}} directs.

guidance.en: Stainless or PVC beads are typical in toilets and other damp areas where galvanized beads can rust through the finish. Cracks commonly appear where render runs unbroken from concrete onto blockwork, so the junction treatment is worth deciding at design stage.

text.en: Prepare backgrounds by removing dust, release agent and laitance, and hack or apply a bonding coat to smooth concrete. Apply render in coats no thicker than the manufacturer recommends, to a total thickness of [[thk]] mm, letting each coat cure before the next. Finished surfaces shall not deviate by more than [[tol]] mm under a 2 m straightedge. Damp-cure cement-based render and protect it from rapid drying.

guidance.en: Hollow and cracked render is a frequent HK defect, usually from thick single coats, poor hacking of smooth concrete, or fast drying in hot weather. Thick render used to correct poor concrete is better addressed by fixing the concrete, particularly on soffits.

text.en: Raised access floor shall be a proprietary system to BS EN 12825 with [[panel]] panels, 600 x 600 mm, at a finished floor height of [[ffh]] mm above the structural slab. Load and deflection performance shall be [[load]], to suit the floor loading in the structural design. Submit the manufacturer's test certificates and layout drawings to {{CA}}.

hint.en: Class to BS EN 12825, confirmed by the structural engineer

guidance.en: Office raised floors in HK are commonly steel-encapsulated cementitious panels at a modest void height for power and data. Check the floor height against door thresholds, lift landings and stair nosings early, as these are often missed in fit-outs.

text.en: Pedestals shall be adjustable steel, fixed to the slab with adhesive or mechanical fixings, [[stringer]]. Bond the floor system to the electrical earthing installation as the electrical engineer specifies, in accordance with the Code of Practice for the Electricity (Wiring) Regulations. Form cut-outs for floor boxes and cables at the positions on the coordinated services layout, with edge trims and [[grommet]] grommets.

guidance.en: Stringers improve lateral stability at greater heights and where panels are lifted often, such as in comms rooms. Cut-outs placed before the furniture layout is fixed are a common source of abortive work.

text.en: Clean the slab and apply a dust-proofing sealer before installing pedestals. Install the floor to the height in {{ref:FIN-RAF-010}}, level within [[tol]] mm over the floor area, with no rocking panels or steps between panels. Provide perimeter support and close gaps at walls and columns with trims. Hand over [[lifters]] panel lifters to {{CA}}.

guidance.en: An unsealed slab sheds dust into the void, which then circulates where the void is used for air supply. Rocking panels are usually traced to uneven pedestal heads or debris, and are cheaper to fix before carpet tiles go down.

text.en: Suspended ceilings shall be [[type]] on a proprietary grid, complying with BS EN 13964 and installed to the system manufacturer's instructions, module [[module]], colour and finish [[colour]]. Gypsum boards shall comply with BS EN 520. Submit samples, technical data and a reflected ceiling plan coordinated with services to {{CA}} for approval.

options.en: mineral fibre lay-in tiles on an exposed grid
jointed gypsum board on a concealed grid
metal clip-in tiles, plain or perforated

guidance.en: Mineral fibre tiles on an exposed grid are the usual office choice for easy access; jointed gypsum board suits feature areas but needs access panels. In HK humidity some mineral fibre tiles sag, so a humidity-resistant grade is commonly chosen where air-conditioning may be off for long periods.

text.en: Suspend the grid from the structural soffit with hangers and fixings to the system manufacturer's design for the loads and soffit type. Do not hang the ceiling from services, ductwork or their supports. Provide additional framing and independent supports for fittings heavier than [[weight]] kg. Install the ceiling level within [[tol]] mm across each room.

guidance.en: Hanging ceilings off ductwork or cable trays is a common site shortcut that causes sagging and makes later services changes difficult. Heavy light fittings and projector brackets are typically supported independently of the grid.

text.en: Provide [[panel]] access panels, not smaller than [[size]] mm, at valves, dampers, fire dampers and other items needing maintenance, at positions agreed on the coordinated layout. Coordinate light fittings, diffusers, sprinklers, detectors and speakers with the grid so they sit centrally in tiles or on regular lines. Do not close the ceiling until the services above have been inspected and released by {{CA}}.

options.en: hinged drop-down panels matching the ceiling finish

guidance.en: Missing or undersized access to fire dampers and valves is a common handover snag and can affect statutory inspections. A coordinated reflected ceiling plan signed off by all trades before the grid goes up is the usual way to avoid it.

text.en: Where the fire safety strategy requires the ceiling to contribute to fire resistance or to limit fire spread, the ceiling shall be a complete tested system achieving [[frr]], installed with the same grid, boards, fixings and penetration details as tested. Comply with the Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings 2011 (2024 Edition) and the project's fire safety strategy. Submit test evidence and the manufacturer's installation conditions to {{CA}} before ordering.

hint.en: As stated in the fire safety strategy

guidance.en: Fire performance belongs to the tested assembly, not to the board alone, so substituting the grid or adding untested access panels and light fittings commonly invalidates it. Leave the rating to the fire engineer or Authorized Person rather than copying it from another project.

text.en: Resilient flooring shall be [[type]] to BS EN ISO 10582, wear layer not less than [[wear]] mm, colour and pattern [[colour]]. Heat-weld sheet joints with matching weld rod [[weld]]. Submit samples and the manufacturer's data to {{CA}} for approval.

options.en: in wet and clinical areas only

guidance.en: LVT is now common in HK office and retail fit-outs for its timber look and easy replacement, while welded sheet suits pantries and clinics where hygiene matters. Wear layer thickness is the main indicator of life, so compare it rather than overall thickness.

text.en: Carpet tiles shall be [[pile]] with [[backing]] backing, size [[size]], classified for [[use]] use to BS EN 1307. Lay in a [[pattern]] pattern. Reaction to fire shall be [[fire]] and shall comply with the project's fire safety strategy. Submit samples and the manufacturer's data to {{CA}} for approval.

options.v: tested to BS 4790 and labelled to BS 5287
options.en: tested to BS 4790 and labelled to BS 5287

by.v: tested to BS 4790 and labelled to BS 5287

guidance.en: Carpet tiles over raised floors are the standard HK office finish because individual tiles lift for access to the void. Quarter-turn laying hides shading between tiles, while monolithic laying shows dye-lot differences clearly.

text.en: Condition flooring and adhesive in the room at service temperature for not less than [[accl]] hours before laying. Lay only on a base meeting {{ref:FIN-SCR-040}} and {{ref:FIN-SCR-050}}, smoothed with a levelling compound where needed. Fix with [[adhesive]] as the flooring manufacturer recommends. Finish edges with [[skirting]] skirting.

options.en: coved vinyl formed up the wall

guidance.en: Laying before materials settle to the air-conditioned temperature commonly leads to gaps and lifting edges, a frequent snag where the air-conditioning is switched on late in a fit-out. Tackifier is typical for carpet tiles on raised floors so they can be lifted.

text.en: Protect completed finishes from damage, staining and traffic until handover, using [[protect]]. Keep protection in place while following trades work and remove it only for final cleaning. Make good or replace damaged finishes to the satisfaction of {{CA}}.

options.en: hardboard or plywood over a breathable sheet
boards in traffic routes and sheet elsewhere

guidance.en: Non-breathable sheet laid over fresh grout or screed can trap moisture and stain the surface. Damage from trolleys and ladders during the final weeks of a fit-out is common, so protection to traffic routes is worth keeping until the end.

text.en: Clean all finishes at completion with methods and products the manufacturers recommend, removing grout haze, adhesive, paint, labels and dust. Do not use acid cleaners on cementitious grout or polished surfaces. Surface treatment after cleaning: [[treat]].

options.en: manufacturer's initial maintenance treatment to resilient flooring

guidance.en: Acid cleaners are commonly used to remove grout haze but etch cement grout and some polished tiles. Unglazed porcelain can absorb stains from early use, so some projects seal it before handover.

text.en: Hand over spare materials from the same production batches as installed: [[spare]] % of the installed quantity of each tile, floor and ceiling finish, labelled and stored where {{CA}} directs. Submit records of products, batch numbers, colours, suppliers and maintenance instructions for the operation and maintenance manual.

guidance.en: Tile and carpet shades vary between batches, so later repairs rarely match without stock from the original run. In HK fit-outs spare stock is commonly handed to building management, so labelling and a recorded location matter.

text.en: Finishes shall be within the following tolerances unless a tighter value is stated for a system. Floors: level within plus or minus [[flevel]] mm of datum, and surface regularity class [[sr]] to BS 8204-1. Walls: plumb within [[wplumb]] mm in any storey height and no deviation greater than [[wflat]] mm under a 2 m straightedge. Ceilings: level within plus or minus [[clevel]] mm across any room. Tiles: lippage not more than [[lip]] mm between adjacent tiles.

guidance.en: One tolerance clause keeps the trade sections short; the values are project choices.

text.en: Wall, ceiling and floor linings in protected exits shall be [[lclass]]. Where a licence condition sets a different class, the stricter of the code and the licence shall apply.

options.en: Class C to BS EN 13501-1 or better
non-combustible, Class A1 to BS EN 13501-1, a project upgrade above the FS Code minimum

guidance.en: FS Code 2011 (2024 Edition) Clauses E13.1(a) and E14.1(a), checked 9 Nov 2026: Class C in protected exits for every Use Class. A1 is offered as a project upgrade. Hotels and guesthouses also need Class 1 or 2 surface spread of flame to BS 476-7 in protected escape routes.

text.en: Linings in corridors shall be [[corr]] and linings in rooms shall be [[room]], unless the fire safety strategy states a higher class.

guidance.en: The FS Code 2024 Edition sets no class for general areas of offices, shops or flats; Class 0 corridors and Class 1 rooms is a landlord norm. For Use Class 3 (including purpose-built clinics, child care centres and elderly homes) Clauses E13.1(b) and E14.1(b) require Class B or above in general areas, so set both fields to Class B.

text.en: Walls of food rooms shall have a smooth, impervious, light-coloured finish of glazed tiles to a height of not less than [[h]] above floor level, with a coved junction at the floor formed by a 45 degree tile or a cove tile, and with epoxy grout. The wall above the tiling and the ceiling shall be finished in washable paint. [[ss]]

options.v: the full height of the wall
options.en: the full height of the wall
Walls behind the cooking line shall be lined with stainless steel as {{ref:MET-SS-010}}.
No stainless steel wall lining is required.

guidance.en: FEHD requires the impervious finish to at least 2 m. Stainless steel behind the cooking line is a common upgrade.

text.en: Floors of food rooms shall be smooth, light-coloured and impervious, laid to falls of [[fall]] to floor drains, with a coved junction at the walls. Kitchens and sculleries shall be [[kslip]] as {{ref:FIN-TILE-030}}. No manhole shall be placed in a food room.

guidance.en: FEHD construction rules. The R12 / P5 kitchen rating has no HK source; it is international practice.

text.en: Ceilings of food rooms shall be washable, moisture resistant and non-combustible.

guidance.en: A non-combustible ceiling avoids a high fire potential finding by FSD.

text.en: Walls of [[rooms]] shall be tiled to a height of not less than [[h]] above floor level.

guidance.en: Licence values differ: guesthouse kitchens 1.2 m, child care washrooms 1 m. School washroom dados are best practice.

text.en: Floors in clinical areas shall be welded sheet vinyl with an integral coved skirting [[cove]] mm high and sealed joints. Carpet and timber shall not be used in clinical areas.

guidance.en: Department of Health guidance for dental clinics; treat as best practice for other clinics.

text.en: Ceilings in operating and procedure rooms shall be sealed metal or sealed board with sealed light fittings and penetrations, and walls shall be finished in a cleanable and disinfectable surface. Ceilings elsewhere in clinical areas shall be clip-in metal.

guidance.en: The DPC Code requires cleanable surfaces in operating rooms; ventilation to ASHRAE 170 drives sealed ceilings.

text.en: Floors used by young children shall be non-slip and easy to clean. Rubber flooring is acceptable in play and activity rooms.

guidance.en: From the SWD/EDB operation manual.

text.en: Sports floors in halls shall comply with BS EN 14904, with line marking for the sports shown on the drawings.

guidance.en: Best practice; no HK source.

text.en: The clear height from finished floor to ceiling shall be not less than [[h]].

by.v: 3 m (2.75 m in premises that are not purpose-built)

guidance.en: Schools: 3 m purpose-built, 2.75 m otherwise (Education Regulations reg. 9). RCHE: 2.5 m, or 2.3 m under beams. Child care: 3 m, or 2.75 m.

text.en: Carpet in protected escape routes shall meet ASTM E648, or BS 5287 when tested to BS 4790, or be pure wool. Carpet with a pile height of not more than 10 mm covering not more than 5 per cent of the protected escape routes on a floor is exempt.

guidance.en: Hotel and guesthouse licensing conditions.

text.en: Industrial floors shall be designed for an imposed load of [[load]] kPa under the Code of Practice for Dead and Imposed Loads 2011 (2021 Edition), with a [[wear]] wearing surface to BS 8204-2 and armoured joints at construction and sawn joints in traffic routes.

guidance.en: Hardener, epoxy and flatness choices have no HK official source.
